summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of histiocytosis X, diabetes insipidus, and recently diagnosed CNS lymphoma was admitted for cycle two of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He had recovered well from a prior craniotomy, with resolution of postoperative aphasia and no residual neurological deficits. The chemotherapy was administered without complications, and he tolerated the treatment well. Hyponatremia, present on admission with a sodium of 127 and later dropping to 120, was managed by holding DDAVP and adjusting IV fluids, with plans to restart DDAVP upon discharge. Methotrexate clearance was confirmed, and leucovorin rescue was completed. He remained seizure-free on levetiracetam, and steroid tapering was initiated by reducing dexamethasone to twice daily. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue oral leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, resume his baseline DDAVP regimen, and follow up in the oncology clinic.
